Contents of https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/129811:
[![@ViveliDuCh](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/50237907?s=40&v=4)](/ViveliDuCh)[](/apps/github-copilot-cli)

Fixes [dotnet#82801](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/82801)

Introduces standardized stream wrappers for text and memory types as
public sealed classes (\`StringStream\`, \`ReadOnlyMemoryStream\`,
\`WritableMemoryStream\`, and \`ReadOnlySequenceStream\` ) as approved in
\[API
review\]([dotnet#82801 (comment)](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/82801#issuecomment-4201484885))
(\[video\]([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T7xc7rARCEw&t=0h9m41s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T7xc7rARCEw&t=0h9m41s))).

### What's included

- \`StringStream\` (\`System.IO\`, CoreLib): non-seekable, read-only stream
that encodes \`string\` or \`ReadOnlyMemory<char>\` on-the-fly. Encoding is
required (no default). Never emits BOMs.
- \`ReadOnlyMemoryStream\` (\`System.IO\`, CoreLib): seekable, read-only
stream over \`ReadOnlyMemory<byte>\`
- \`WritableMemoryStream\` (\`System.IO\`, CoreLib): seekable, read-write
stream over \`Memory<byte>\` with fixed capacity
- \`ReadOnlySequenceStream\` (\`System.Buffers\`, System.Memory): seekable,
read-only stream over \`ReadOnlySequence<byte>\`
- Ref assembly updates for \`System.Runtime\` and \`System.Memory\`
- Updated 3 internal call sites (\`ReadOnlyMemoryContent\`,
\`XmlPreloadedResolver\`, \`JsonXmlDataContract\`) to use the new types
- Conformance and behavioral tests for all 4 types

### Implementation notes

- All types are \`public sealed\` with direct constructors: the review
moved away from factory methods on \`Stream\` to avoid derived-type
IntelliSense noise
- \`StringStream\` encodes directly into the caller's buffer in \`Read()\`
rather than using an internal byte buffer
- \`ReadOnlyMemoryStream\` and \`WritableMemoryStream\` derive from
\`MemoryStream\`.
- \`TryGetBuffer\` returns false and \`GetBuffer\` throws on the memory
stream types (no \`publiclyVisible\` support for now)

### Limitations

- The internal
\[shared-source\]([https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/Common/src/System/IO/ReadOnlyMemoryStream.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/Common/src/System/IO/ReadOnlyMemoryStream.cs))
\`ReadOnlyMemoryStream\` in \`Common/\` cannot be fully replaced:

This article categorizes each breaking change as _binary incompatible_ or _source incompatible_, or as a _behavioral change_:

*   **Binary incompatible** - When run against the new runtime or component, existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.

Here are the **4 breaking changes** in .NET 11 that affect your app:

---

### 1. GZipStream empty output check is broken
**`DeflateStream and GZipStream write headers and footers for empty payload`**

Previously, compressing zero bytes produced a 0-length output. Now it writes valid GZip headers/footers (**20 bytes for GZip**, 2 for Deflate) even with no data. Your `output.Length == 0` check for "no data" will **never be true anymore**.

**Fix:** Check the original data length before compression, or special-case empty input to skip compression entirely.

---

### 2. TAR archives with invalid checksums now throw
**`TAR-reading APIs verify header checksums when reading`**

`TarReader.GetNextEntry()` now validates checksums and throws `InvalidDataException` on mismatch. Your legacy hand-crafted TARs with bad checksums will **fail at read time**.

**Fix:** Wrap reads in `try/catch (InvalidDataException)`, or fix the legacy tool to produce valid checksums.

---

### 3. ZipArchive.CreateAsync no longer lazy-loads entries
**`ZipArchive.CreateAsync eagerly loads ZIP archive entries`**

Previously, `CreateAsync` deferred reading entries until you accessed `.Entries` (potentially doing sync reads). Now it **eagerly reads the entire central directory** during `CreateAsync`. This means:
- Errors from malformed entries surface at `CreateAsync` time, not `.Entries` access
- No more lazy loading behavior to depend on
- Memory for all entries is allocated upfront

**Fix:** Move error handling to the `CreateAsync` call. For very large archives, be aware of the upfront memory cost.

---

### 4. MemoryStream near max capacity — **no specific .NET 11 breaking change found**

I did not find a documented .NET 11 breaking change for `MemoryStream` maximum capacity. However, note that .NET 11 introduces new `ReadOnlyMemoryStream` and `WritableMemoryStream` types (deriving from `MemoryStream`) which could be worth considering as alternatives. Your existing large-allocation `MemoryStream` usage should continue to work as before.
